column1: # The function-quality audit ledger — coverage AND open findings, one row per .c file
# in src/. No exceptions: tools/guardrails.sh checks this list against the tree in both
# directions, so a file can never be silently skipped — a new .c file has to be
# classified here before `make guardrails` passes again.
# THE STANDARD — four questions per function, asked when a file is audited:
#   1. Does it name one real domain concept? (Not "these lines appeared together twice.")
#   2. Is its signature minimal and honest? No dead parameters — a signature that names
#      a parameter it never reads over-claims its edges, the mirror of a missing const.
#      Broad-and-const is fine; broad-and-mutable is not. The write set drives the count.
#   3. Is claimed purity real? For anything under a *_pure/ directory: no static mutable
#      state, no I/O, no RNG, no clock, every pointer const. The directory name is a
#   4. Is the duplication genuine? Extract only where a real, nameable concept exists —
#      if merging two similar blocks needs a mode flag to keep them apart, they were two
#      rules that happened to look alike, and merging makes the code less tractable.
#   audited   read against the four questions above
#   open      not audited yet, and nothing blocks auditing it
#   deferred  a scheduled slice rewrites or deletes the file, so auditing it now is
#             churn — the audit is part of THAT slice's exit criteria instead
# THE NOTE COLUMN carries open findings — things a read turned up that were not fixed
# on the spot, marked "OPEN FINDING:". They live here rather than in prose so they sit
# next to the file they are about and cannot drift away from the tree. A finding that
# gets fixed leaves this file; what it taught goes to the docs' history instead.
